newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget gap narrows slightly in November.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget gap narrows slightly in November.

text.p: The shortfall between the government's income and its spending narrowed slightly to $37.88 billion in November from a gap of $40.26 billion in October, the Treasury Department said Friday.
The monthly deficit also was down from a year earlier, in November 1995 when there was a $38.45 shortfall.

But so far during the first two months of fiscal 1997 ending next Sept. 30, the cumulative deficit was up 28 percent to $78.14 billion from $61.03 billion in the comparable first two months of fiscal 1996.
The Clinton admininstration has forecast a full-year deficit in fiscal 1997 of $125.73 billion, which would be an increase from the deficit of $107.28 billion posted in fiscal 1996.
Total spending in November was $135.8 billion, down from $140.32 billion spent in October but up from $128.54 billion in November 1995.
Income, primarily from taxation, declined to $97.92 billion last month from $100.06 billion in October. But it was up from November 1995 when the government took in $90.09 billion of revenes.
The Treasury said November revenues were boosted by a one-time special assessment of $4.5 billion collected from the thrift industry to set up a Savings Association Insurance Fund.

In addition, it said pay for active duty military personnel, veterans' benefits and supplemental social security payments that were scheduled for Dec. 1 were accelerated to Nov. 29, which pushed up outlays last month.

The White House already is working on budget proposals for fiscal 1998, which starts next Oct. 1. President Clinton is to submit the 1998 budget proposals to Congress early next February shortly after his inauguration to a second term as President.
